local_checks.invariant: An OTP proves the account: random 6-digit code, HMAC bound to user id, 10-minute expiry, single use, bound to securityEpoch, counted failures and lock at 5
local_checks.result: Holds. newCode uses randomInt (policy.ts:30-31). digestCode is HMAC(OTP_SECRET, userId:code) (policy.ts:20-24) and is compared in constant time (policy.ts:25-29). verifyCode locks the user row FOR UPDATE (otp.ts:83-87), rejects a missing, used, expired or other-epoch challenge (otp.ts:100-106), counts failures with failureResult (otp.ts:107-123), and marks the code used in the same transaction (otp.ts:125-128). The session is issued only through createProvenSession with the proven epoch, which the session-create hook re-checks under FOR UPDATE (index.ts:47-57, 123-156). No OTP bypass found.

local_checks.invariant: Recovery codes are high-entropy, one-time, bound to the technical account, and unlock without granting a session
local_checks.result: Holds. newRecoveryCode is 24 random bytes (policy.ts:32), stored as an HMAC digest bound to the target id (accounts.ts:321-329). useRecoveryCode locks the user row and the code row, sets usedAt, bumps the epoch and revokes access (accounts.ts:332-374). It returns only {success:true}, so login still needs an OTP to the account's mailbox. Recovery has no failure counter, but brute force of 192-bit codes is infeasible.

local_checks.invariant: Pre-auth responses give the same answer for registered and unregistered addresses (decision 177, user decision; code comment otp.ts:32)
local_checks.result: Violated. There are three source-visible differences. sealSecret has no AAD binding the ciphertext to the outbox row (id/recipient/kind), so anyone with DB write access could move a sealed code between rows. Bind it with cipher.setAAD(`${id}:${recipientAccountId}:${kind}`).

When MAIL_TRANSPORT is not 'brevo', deliverNextEmail returns before closeExpired (email.ts:282-303). Expired login/email-change messages then keep encryptedSecret in email_outbox and in backups indefinitely. The codes are expired and key-sealed, but clearing them in a maintenance step independent of the transport would limit retention.

revokeAccess (src/server/auth/accounts.ts:129-148) cancels only login-code mail, not pending email-change code mail. The codes are unusable after the epoch bump, but cancelling them as well avoids sending a dead code.

requestEmailChange/confirmEmailChange (src/server/auth/email-change.ts:77-90, 211-219) update every email-change outbox row of the account regardless of status, which rewrites already-sent or failed history to 'cancelled' (confirm also omits updatedAt). local_checks.invariant: Restore does not silently reintroduce state current policy forbids beyond what the product accepted

local_checks.result: Retention removes only verified backup_run rows the current DB knows; after a restore, later Drive backups and the renamed <db>_before_restore_<time> database fall outside rotation. Both are documented manual-cleanup steps (operations.md:367,371). Hardening only.

local_checks.invariant: Restore CLI output and stored reports carry no personal data or key material

notes: Lead: deletion-log chain is unkeyed SHA-256 (domain/deletion-log.ts:37-48); who can write the local file / Drive copy and is that a lower-trust principal than the operator? Drive upload follows provider Location header with bearer token (backup-storage.ts:299-314).

hardening: The deletion log chain is unkeyed SHA-256 (src/domain/deletion-log.ts:37-48). verifyDeletionLog accepts a copy that is merely ahead (src/server/operations/deletion-log.ts:344-353, warning only), and a fresh volume trusts the storage copy alone. Appending recomputed lines to one copy is therefore enough, despite decision 196's claim that forgery needs both copies. applyLoggedDeletions then erases with force, including manager-linked soldiers (restore-deletions.ts:94-98). The writer must hold the dedicated Drive account or the server volume. That is the same trust needed to replace backup content: age does not authenticate the sender, and locateBackup without a live DB trusts the provider sha256 (restore.ts:236-249). Consider a MAC keyed with material kept beside the age identity.

After restore, Drive backups newer than the restore point and the renamed <db>_before_restore_<time> database are outside the 30-copy rotation and are never removed automatically (backup.ts:420-432 rotates only DB-known runs; restore.ts:1123). Documented as manual cleanup in docs/operations.md:367,371. A tracked reminder or expiry would bound how long erased data persists there.
command_results rows are never purged (only eraseSoldier rewrites them), so every stored result, including manager previews with personal data, is retained indefinitely and copied into every backup.

Drive resumable upload sends the bearer token to the Location header returned by Google (backup-storage.ts:299-314). Asserting that the URL origin is https://www.googleapis.com before following it would remove reliance on response integrity.

local_checks.invariant: settleDue credits only published duties that have ended, from fields a soldier cannot write, at most once per assignment
local_checks.result: settleDue reads assignment.points and data.performedEnd. Only manager execution, correction and swap-after-start handlers write these (execution.ts, swaps.ts:1124-1131 driven by a manager's handoverAt); no soldier path writes them. It credits once: the query filters status='reserved', the row then moves to 'credited', and postScore deduplicates on ledger sourceKey performance:<assignmentId>. A seat held by a deleted soldier waits for deletionDecidedAt. No soldier-controlled crediting path was found.

local_checks.invariant: A unit-maintenance retry (retryLimit 5) or repeated run does not duplicate notices, mail or credits
local_checks.result: All maintenance steps run in one unitTransaction under the global lock, so a failure rolls back everything. Departures are deduplicated per soldier and releaseDate, round notices by round_notice markers per generation and phase, and duty reminders by a lastRunAt watermark. The outbox insert uses onConflictDoNothing on eventKey. drainMail runs after commit, and lease and ownLease guard against double delivery. Retries are idempotent.

local_checks.result: roundEmailRelevant (round-recipients.ts:116-126) drops managers and recipients who fail canAccessAfterService. dutyReminderRelevant (duty-reminder-checks.ts:47-67) requires a non-deleted account, hasAccess() and an active seat. deliverNextEmail calls both at email.ts:356-378. These are covered, and they form the sibling control that the manager-alert kinds lack.

local_checks.invariant: Rank reminders produced by the worker do not mail or expose data to non-managers
local_checks.result: refreshRankReminders writes only rank_reminder records. It never calls enqueueEmail, and it skips soldiers who are deleted or whose service has ended. No outbox exposure was found.

local_checks.invariant: Manager-only alert mail (departure, deletion, restore) reaches only managers who still have access; an ex-member whose service ended stops receiving unit data
local_checks.result: This invariant is violated. announceDepartures picks recipients by role=='manager' && !deletedAt (departures.ts:74-77). Soldier deletion picks by role only (soldier-deletion.ts:641-645), and announceRestore by role and deletedAt (restore.ts:718-723). None checks service end, although accountAvailable (accounts.ts:42-55) refuses that same manager on every request. At delivery, deliverNextEmail checks only recipient.deletedAt (email.ts:328-333) and preferences, with no relevance check for these kinds. Decision 170 (docs/open-decisions.md:399) says the notice goes to every *active* manager.

local_checks.result: Run with dummy data in the offline sandbox. FORMER_ACCOUNT_AVAILABLE false, role manager. After another soldier departs, one pending departure outbox row is queued for the former manager. deliverNextEmail then sends it to 00901@example.invalid with subject 'סיום שירות', and the body contains SUBJECT-SOLDIER.

local_checks.invariant: Demoting a manager to soldier stops later disclosure of manager-only alerts queued before the demotion
local_checks.result: Not a separate disclosure. setRole bumps securityEpoch and revokes sessions but does not cancel queued outbox rows, so a departure or deletion mail queued before the demotion can still go out within its 24 h expiry. That mail matches the site notification addressed to the same account, and state.ts:125-162/365-374 keeps that notice visible to the account after demotion. The event was also created while the recipient was authorized. Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Request-decision mail goes only to the requesting soldier's own account and omits free-text reasons
local_checks.result: Recipients come from user.soldierId == data.soldierId && !deletedAt, so the mail is the soldier's own request. It is sent only while the duty has not ended, and the body uses emailBody, which drops free-text reasons (decision 177). No cross-principal data is involved.
